note: The UN Secretary-General condemned an airstrike that reportedly killed at least 50 people at a market in Rakhine state and called for accountability. Air attacks on civilian sites deepen the civil war and add pressure on neighbours already receiving returned refugees.

title: DRC peace deals fail to halt M23 fighting as Rwanda tensions rise
note: The UN Security Council heard that clashes between Congolese forces and M23 rebels continue in the east despite a series of peace agreements, with rising tension between the DRC and Rwanda. The country's worst recorded Ebola outbreak, above 3,900 deaths, compounds the crisis.
limitations: The summary of a live Security Council session does not give casualty figures for the fighting or attribute responsibility for violations. Drafted by an automated daily job from the linked report; not yet reviewed.

title: Russian missile campaign leaves Ukraine's steelworks all but halted
note: The BBC reports that Ukraine's remaining steelworks, a vital part of its economy, have nearly ground to a halt under relentless attacks. Damage to heavy industry cuts export earnings and domestic arms and reconstruction capacity, lengthening the war's economic toll.
limitations: The summary gives no output figures or count of damaged plants, and the assessment rests on a single outlet. Drafted by an automated daily job from the linked report; not yet reviewed.

title: UN chief calls this the most dangerous nuclear moment since Cold War
note: At the observance of the International Day for the Total Elimination of Nuclear Weapons, the UN Secretary-General urged replacing threats with dialogue. Speakers cited expanding arsenals, eroding arms control and strikes on nuclear infrastructure in Iran and Ukraine.
limitations: This is a rhetorical assessment in a speech and does not measure any change in actual nuclear risk. Drafted by an automated daily job from the linked report; not yet reviewed.

title: Hormuz crude flows recover but tanker insurance and risk keep costs high
note: Al Jazeera reports crude flows through the Strait of Hormuz have recovered, though tanker insurance costs and geopolitical risk still block a return to normal. The analysis asks whether Iran is losing its leverage over the chokepoint.

title: Funding cuts put 8.3 million refugees at risk of losing UN aid
note: The UN refugee agency is scaling back core programmes as its available funding fell from 5.2 billion to 3.9 billion US dollars between 2024 and 2025. Nearly 8.3 million displaced and stateless people face losing vital assistance, which raises the risk of onward movement and instability.
